es: Condensar un párrafo narrativo en un texto nominal de unas 60 palabras: convertir acciones en sustantivos, unir causa y efecto con caused, led to o due to y retomar con this delay.

teaching.en: A long delay in construction can give rise to anger among local families, especially when a shortage of builders is to blame.
teaching.es: Un retraso largo en la construcción puede dar lugar a enojo entre las familias del barrio, sobre todo si la culpa es de la escasez de constructores.
teaching.explanationEs: delay y shortage condensan dos acciones; give rise to une causa y efecto como un verbo de causa formal.
segments: A long delay in construction can give rise to anger among
local families, especially when a shortage of builders is to blame.
teaching.audioText: A long delay in construction can give rise to anger among local families, especially when a shortage of builders is to blame.

teaching.en: The main consequence of the delay was a cost overrun, which seems to stem from a shortage of materials rather than poor planning.
teaching.es: La consecuencia principal del retraso fue un sobrecosto, que parece derivarse de la escasez de materiales y no de una mala planificación.
teaching.explanationEs: consequence of + sustantivo; stem from presenta el origen de algo con cautela (seems to).
segments: The main consequence of the delay was a cost overrun, which seems
to stem from a shortage of materials rather than poor planning.
teaching.audioText: The main consequence of the delay was a cost overrun, which seems to stem from a shortage of materials rather than poor planning.

teaching.en: The council's investment in the library could contribute to a real change in the district, but only if the construction is finished on time.
teaching.es: La inversión del ayuntamiento en la biblioteca podría provocar un cambio real en el distrito, pero solo si la construcción termina a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: investment + in; contribute to presenta la inversión como una de las causas, no la única.
segments: The council's investment in the library could contribute to a real change
in the district, but only if the construction is finished on time.

teaching.en: In the wake of the delay, the outcome of the project was uncertain, although the final result was positive.
teaching.es: Tras el retraso, el resultado final del proyecto era incierto, aunque el balance fue positivo.
teaching.explanationEs: in the wake of + grupo nominal sitúa un hecho como consecuencia de otro; outcome resume cómo terminó todo.

project was uncertain, although the final result was positive.

prompt.es: Elige la versión condensada de la frase sobre los constructores.

The builders' delay, due to the families' anger, caused a late opening of the library.

feedback.es: La versión correcta conserva la cadena causal (retraso, apertura tardía, enojo) con un sustantivo y un verbo de causa; las otras invierten quién causa qué.

hint.es: Comprueba que el retraso sea la causa y el enojo la consecuencia, no al revés.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige su versión condensada más fiel.

choices.text: A shortage of workers delayed the opening of the library, and the anger of the families led to more visitors and more reading.
A shortage of workers delayed the opening of the library, which caused anger and complaints but has led to more visitors and more reading.
Extra spending by the council delayed the opening of the library, which caused anger among families but brought more visitors in the end.

feedback.es: La versión fiel conserva la causa real (la escasez de trabajadores) y el orden de los efectos; las otras atribuyen el retraso o las visitas a causas equivocadas.

origin.audio: Last spring the builders were late because there were not enough workers. As a result, the library opened two months behind schedule. The families were angry and sent many complaints to the council. The council then spent more money than planned, but today the library is full of visitors, and the children read more than before.

answer.text: The investment in the library brought about a rise in visitors

feedback.es: Investment es el sujeto nominal y brought about, el verbo de causa; a rise in visitors es el efecto.

prompt.es: Condensa el informe de la biblioteca en un texto nominal de unas 150 palabras.

answer.text: The construction of the new neighbourhood library was delayed by two years, owing to a shortage of skilled workers in the region. This delay gave rise to anger among local families and to a wave of complaints addressed to the council. In the wake of these problems, a sharp rise in the price of materials, which stemmed from the suppliers' failure to deliver on time, led to a cost overrun, since the council also had to pay the workers for extra months. The newspaper's questions prompted the council to promise an investigation into the lack of planning. The outcome, however, has been positive: the opening of the library in September has brought about a steady increase in visitors, now above a thousand a week, and a marked improvement in the children's reading. In the director's view, the main consequence of the delay was a lesson in careful planning, and the families' complaints deserve credit for the council's response.
accepted: The construction of the new neighbourhood library was delayed by two years, owing to a shortage of skilled workers in the region. This delay gave rise to anger among local families and to a wave of complaints addressed to the council. In the wake of these problems, a sharp rise in the price of materials, which stemmed from the suppliers' failure to deliver on time, led to a cost overrun, since the council also had to pay the workers for extra months. The newspaper's questions prompted the council to promise an investigation into the lack of planning. The outcome, however, has been positive: the opening of the library in September has brought about a steady increase in visitors, now above a thousand a week, and a marked improvement in the children's reading. In the director's view, the main consequence of the delay was a lesson in careful planning, and the families' complaints deserve credit for the council's response.

A shortage of skilled workers in the region caused a two-year delay in the construction of the new library, and the delay led to anger among families and to many complaints. The rise in the price of materials, due to late deliveries from the suppliers, resulted in a cost overrun, because the council had to pay the workers for extra months. After newspaper questions about the lack of planning, the council promised an investigation. The outcome is nevertheless good: since the opening in September, the number of visitors has risen above a thousand a week, and the children read much more than before. According to the director, the consequence of the delay has been better planning, and the families' complaints deserve thanks for the council's response.

feedback.es: Un buen texto condensado nombra el retraso y su causa, enlaza las consecuencias con verbos de causa o due to y conserva el resultado final, usando nominalizaciones.

origin.text: Two years ago the council decided to build a new library in our neighbourhood, and everybody was pleased. However, the builders were late because there were not enough skilled workers in the region, so the work fell behind schedule. As a result, the library opened two years late, and many families were angry and sent letters of complaint to the council. While they waited, the price of materials rose sharply, because the suppliers could not deliver on time, and the council had to pay the workers for extra months. In the wake of these problems, the newspaper asked why nobody had planned for the risk, and the council promised that it would investigate the matter. Finally, the library opened in September. The council had spent much more money than it had planned, but the result was good: every week more than a thousand people visit, and the children read much more than before. Looking back, the director says that the delay taught the council to plan more carefully, and that the families who complained deserve thanks, because their letters made the council act.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la directora sobre las quejas de las familias?

choices.text: That the council was to blame for the shortage of builders.
That the families should have complained much earlier in the project.
That the complaints improved the council's planning, despite the anger.
That the delay was a failure that nobody could have prevented.

feedback.es: Dice que las quejas obligaron a revisar la planificación y que el enojo fue una consecuencia que debió acogerse antes: valora su efecto positivo.

origin.text: It is easy to describe the delay as a failure, but the outcome tells a different story. The shortage of builders was beyond our control; the complaints of the families, however, were not, and they forced us to revise our planning. In that sense, the anger was a consequence we should have welcomed earlier.

prompt.es: Completa: «El aumento de costos parece derivarse de la escasez de materiales.»

feedback.es: Stem from presenta la causa como origen probable; el seems to de la frase añade cautela.

origin.text: The rise in costs seems to ___ from a shortage of materials rather than from poor planning, although the council has not yet confirmed this.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El sobrecosto fue una consecuencia directa del largo retraso.»

answer.text: The cost overrun was a direct consequence of the long delay

feedback.es: The cost overrun es el sujeto; a direct consequence of + el retraso nombra la causa.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué actitud deja ver la alcaldesa.

choices.text: She accepts that the delay did harm but avoids taking the blame.
She regrets the delay deeply and apologises to every family.
She denies that the delay caused any real problem at all.

feedback.es: Reconoce la pérdida de confianza, pero no pide disculpas y habla de lecciones aprendidas: admite el daño sin asumir la culpa.

origin.audio: In her speech, the mayor said that the outcome was positive, but she added that the main consequence of the delay had been a loss of trust. She did not apologise; she said only that lessons had been learned, and she thanked the families for their patience.
